source.title: Optimal Rates of Kernel Ridge Regression under Source Condition in Large Dimensions
source.authors: Haobo Zhang; Yicheng Li; Weihao Lu; Qian Lin

record.tranche_reason: The paper is fully available and derives KRR generalization-error rates, but its multiple-descent results concern rates across the sample-to-dimension scaling exponent γ, not the claim versions’ model-size, epoch, or interpolation-threshold tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own theoretical KRR rate curves with periodic plateaus and multiple descent as γ varies. Those curves are not direct measurements of test error rising when sample count increases near an interpolation threshold. Its citations and discussion of earlier studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper is a theoretical derivation of exact asymptotic convergence rates for optimally regularized KRR with inner product kernels on the sphere, where n ≍ d^γ. Its 'multiple descent' refers to peaks in the rate exponent r (error ≍ n^r) as γ varies. The paper also states that error decreases monotonically as γ grows (Figure 2, error ≍ d^r). It reports no test error rising with model size, epochs or samples near an interpolation threshold. It does not vary label noise or tune regularization against a ridgeless baseline, and it does not count effective parameters. So it bears on no version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. One clarification should be added: the multiple descent is a property of the rate exponent along γ, under the optimally chosen regularization parameter.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives theoretical KRR rates for sphere kernels as sample size scales with dimension; it does not reproduce a deep-network size or epoch sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The rate-curve shape depends on source smoothness s and kernel choice; for 0 < s ≤ 1/2, the proved range excludes γ ≤ 3s/[2(s+1)].

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical rate curves for optimally regularized KRR on the sphere show periodic plateaus and multiple descent in the n-exponent as γ varies (n ≍ d^γ). The curve shape depends on source smoothness s. For s > 1, KRR has a saturation effect: it falls short of the minimax rate for some γ ranges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In large-dimensional KRR with n ≍ d^γ, optimally tuned asymptotic error rates show periodic plateaus and multiple-descent peaks in the n-exponent at γ values set by source smoothness s, while error still decreases monotonically with n.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and asymptotic, under specified kernel, distribution, noise, and source-condition assumptions; it does not report direct test-error measurements or test the claim’s interpolation-threshold behavior. For 0 < s ≤ 1/2, the paper proves rates only for γ > 3s/[2(s+1)].
record.rows_left_out: No rows for cited results from other studies. The NTK subsection gives related KRR rate theorems, but its results do not establish the claim’s specified test-error behavior near an interpolation threshold.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep and no deep networks.
No finite-sample test-error curve near an interpolation threshold. Under optimal λ the paper's d-exponent rates decrease monotonically with γ.
No capacity sweep past an interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.

No label-noise variation. There is no comparison of a ridgeless or untuned setting with optimal regularization. The multiple peaks are rate-exponent peaks under optimal λ, not noise-driven test-error peaks.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters.

record.verdict_notes: This is a pure theory preprint with no experiments. The 'multiple descent' terminology refers to the shape of the asymptotic rate exponent, not to test error rising. It should not be read as evidence for or against V3 or V6. The NTK subsection (two-layer ReLU NTK) gives analogous rate theorems without proofs; it also bears on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and peak near the training-set interpolation threshold in deep networks.
Whether actual test error rises as the number of samples increases near an interpolation threshold; the paper instead studies asymptotic rates as n ≍ d^γ.
Capacity sweeps past an interpolation point across model classes.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.
Dependence of peaks on label noise or variance, multiple peaks caused by noise, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
Whether counting complexity by an effective parameter number turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression (KRR) with an inner product kernel on the sphere
rows.operation_detail: Derived asymptotic generalization-error convergence rates as n ≍ d^γ and described the resulting rate curves across γ.

conditions.value: uniform distribution on the sphere; n ≍ d^γ

rows.measure: Asymptotic convergence rate of expected generalization error, varying with γ
rows.value: The rate curve is described as having periodic plateaus and multiple descent; for 0 < s ≤ 1 it matches the minimax lower-rate curve. The stated minimax-rate peaks are at γ = p + ps and isolated valleys at γ = p + ps + s, p ∈ N+; the KRR rate curve is stated to be the same for 0 < s ≤ 1.
rows.note: This is an asymptotic rate curve across sample-to-dimension scaling, not a reported increase in test error from adding samples at fixed settings near an interpolation threshold. For 0 < s ≤ 1/2, the paper proves rates only for γ > 3s/[2(s+1)].
rows.check: Link and state are correct. One clarification: the peaks are in the n-exponent of the rate. The paper states rates decrease as γ increases, 'performance becomes better when the sample size n grows'. So this is not a non-monotone error curve.

rows.subject: kernel ridge regression (KRR) with an inner product kernel on the sphere
rows.operation_detail: Derived asymptotic generalization-error convergence rates as n ≍ d^γ and described the resulting rate curves across γ.

conditions.value: uniform distribution on the sphere; n ≍ d^γ

rows.measure: Asymptotic convergence rate of expected generalization error, varying with γ
rows.value: The paper describes multiple descent in the KRR rate curve. For 1 < s < 2, it states peaks at γ = p + ps̃, isolated valleys at γ = p + ps̃ + 1, and hillsides at γ = p + ps̃ + 2s̃ − 1, p ∈ N+; for s ≥ 2, it states peaks at γ = 3p and isolated valleys at γ = 3p + 1, p ∈ N+ (s̃ = min{s, 2}). It also reports a new saturation effect: KRR fails to attain the minimax lower bound for certain γ ranges.
rows.note: These are theoretical rate-shape results across γ. They do not identify an interpolation threshold or establish actual test-error increases caused by adding samples near such a threshold.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The same clarification applies: the multiple descent is in the exponent r with error ≍ n^r, under optimally chosen λ. It is not an increase in test error with more data, and there is no interpolation threshold.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
